what_happened: The job to split briefs.rs by moving the boundary-scan code into a submodule was rejected at the final verdict. One of 5 acceptance criteria was unmet: briefs.rs must have fewer than 1500 production lines, with the moved code in briefs/boundary.rs. The blocker finding says briefs.rs is still 2287 production lines and has a 217-line function, over the code-health limits. The two major findings say the plan was sized from the request's quoted figure instead of a measurement, and the accepted reading did not match the request. No checks are listed as failed.
cause: Requests that quote a file size or a function length are accepted as true. Nothing measures the file in the current snapshot before the reading is accepted, and nothing makes the producer re-measure before it finishes. So the plan was sized from a stale or wrong figure. The slice that was moved was too small to bring the file under its limit. The criteria checked that the code moved, but the real goal was a line count under the limit. This is the third rejection of this kind in a row for file-split jobs, and no protection exists for the class.
prevention: Add a code check for size-reduction jobs. Before the reading is accepted, Athena measures each named file's production lines and its longest function in the current snapshot and puts the measured numbers into the reading. The reading must size the slice to reach the limit. The producer must also run the same measurement after its change and report it, and the job cannot finish if the file is still over the limit. The check should not depend on the request's quoted number.
proposed_request: Split crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs so that it is under the code-health limits. First measure the file in the current snapshot: production lines (before `#[cfg(test)]`) and the longest functions. Do not rely on any figure quoted elsewhere. Then move enough code, starting with the boundary-scan code, into submodules such as crates/athena-context/src/briefs/boundary.rs to bring briefs.rs below 1500 production lines. Break up any function longer than 200 lines, including the 217-line function. briefs.rs must declare `mod boundary;` and use `pub use` for its public items, so callers are unchanged. Behavior must not change. Fix any existing test that reads the moved files as text. Acceptance: (1) briefs.rs has fewer than 1500 production lines, with the measured before and after counts in the job report; (2) no function in briefs.rs or the new submodules is longer than 200 lines; (3) cargo test, clippy and fmt are clean; (4) CHANGELOG.md has an entry.
